name: tomato
sowing_season: Kharif: June–July | Rabi: Oct–Nov | Summer: Jan–Feb
harvest_season: Continuous picking from 60–120 days after transplanting
soil: Well-drained sandy loam to loam, pH 6.0–7.0, rich in organic matter

stages.name: Nursery / Seedling
stages.description: Seeds sown in raised nursery beds. Seedlings raised for 25–30 days.
stages.irrigation: Light sprinkler irrigation twice daily. Keep moist.
stages.fertilizer: Mix FYM 2 kg per sq metre in nursery. Seed treatment with Trichoderma.
watch_for: Whitefly transmitting Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV)
tips: Cover nursery with insect-proof net to prevent whitefly

stages.name: Transplanting / Establishment
stages.description: Seedlings (25–30 days old) transplanted to main field.
stages.irrigation: Irrigate immediately after transplanting. Then every 4–5 days by drip or furrow.
stages.fertilizer: Basal: 50 kg DAP + 25 kg MOP + 10 tonnes FYM per acre. Top dress 20 kg Urea at 20 days.
tips: Stake plants with bamboo to support fruiting branches

stages.name: Vegetative Growth
stages.description: Rapid stem and leaf growth. Flower buds forming.
stages.irrigation: Regular irrigation every 5–7 days. Drip preferred.
stages.fertilizer: Second top dress: 20 kg Urea + 10 kg MOP at 45 days after transplanting.
watch_for: Early blight (brown concentric rings on lower leaves)
tips: Remove suckers to direct energy to fruiting
Spray Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre for early blight prevention

stages.name: Flowering
stages.irrigation: Maintain consistent soil moisture. Irregular watering causes blossom drop.
stages.fertilizer: Foliar spray: 0.5% Boron + 0.5% Calcium at first flowering.
watch_for: Fruit borer (Helicoverpa) laying eggs on flowers
Blossom drop due to heat or moisture stress
tips: Blossom drop is common in hot weather — spray Planofix (NAA) 4.5 ml/15 litres
Do not apply pesticides when flowers are open

stages.name: Fruit Set / Development
stages.description: Fruits setting and growing in size.
stages.irrigation: Regular irrigation critical — irregular watering causes blossom end rot and cracking.
stages.fertilizer: Third top dress: 15 kg Urea + 10 kg MOP for fruit development.
watch_for: Blossom end rot (dark sunken spot at fruit tip)
tips: Spray Spinosad 0.3 ml/litre for fruit borer
Blossom end rot is caused by calcium deficiency + irregular irrigation

stages.name: Harvest
stages.description: Fruits turning from green to red. Continuous picking over 4–8 weeks.
stages.fertilizer: No major fertilizer. Continue foliar sprays if needed.
watch_for: Post-harvest fruit rot if handling is rough
Cracking due to heavy rain after dry spell
tips: Harvest at breaker stage (turning pink) for distant markets
Harvest fully red for local sale or processing
Pick every 3–4 days for continuous yield

common_pests.name: Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa)
common_pests.symptoms: Circular holes in fruits, caterpillar visible inside

common_pests.name: Whitefly
common_pests.symptoms: Tiny white insects under leaves, sticky honeydew, yellowing

common_pests.name: Spider Mites
common_pests.symptoms: Fine webbing under leaves, bronze/rusty discoloration
common_pests.control: Abamectin 0.5 ml/litre or wettable sulphur 3 g/litre

common_diseases.name: Early Blight (Alternaria)
common_diseases.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target board) on older leaves

common_diseases.name: Late Blight (Phytophthora)
common_diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked dark brown patches on leaves and stem, white mould in humid conditions
common_diseases.control: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre; act fast — spreads rapidly

common_diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt
common_diseases.symptoms: Sudden wilting of entire plant, brown discoloration inside stem, slimy ooze
common_diseases.control: No cure — remove and destroy plant; drench surrounding area with Copper oxychloride
